builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: PCC: Pivotal Channel Compensation for Layer Pruning of Large Language Models
summary: PCC replaces costlier post-pruning compensation (such as fine-tuning-based recovery) with small learnable linear transformations applied to a few pivotal channels at the pruning interface after removing whole transformer layers. It costs a small number of extra parameters and a modest training pass for the compensation matrices, and it presupposes that layer pruning is already being used. It can fail if the pivotal-channel concentration assumption does not hold for the target model, if the pruned model's degradation exceeds what channel-level linear compensation can recover, or if the compression target does not actually require layer pruning rather than quantization or KV-cache reduction.
rationale: PCC is a low-cost post-hoc recovery step that only matters if the team already performs or plans layer pruning on deployed models, so its value is conditional on that specific compression workflow and should be validated on the team's own models and tasks.
technique: Pivotal channel compensation after layer pruning

claims.statement: PCC replaces costlier post-pruning compensation (such as fine-tuning-based recovery) with small learnable linear transformations applied to a few pivotal channels at the pruning interface after removing whole transformer layers. It costs a small number of extra parameters and a modest training pass for the compensation matrices, and it presupposes that layer pruning is already being used. It can fail if the pivotal-channel concentration assumption does not hold for the target model, if the pruned model's degradation exceeds what channel-level linear compensation can recover, or if the compression target does not actually require layer pruning rather than quantization or KV-cache reduction.

The paper reports significant and consistent performance improvements on language modeling and zero-shot question answering across various LLMs when PCC is applied to state-of-the-art layer pruning methods, with fewer additional parameters and lower training cost than existing compensation methods; no specific numeric magnitude is given in the abstract.
